subject: home_science
chapter_title: Management of Support Services, Institutions and Programmes for Children, Youth and Elderly

concepts.title: Why Society Builds Support Services
concepts.definition: A family, though the basic unit of society, cannot deliver every specialised need of its members -- schooling, hospitals, training and recreation -- so communities raise extra structures, and the state steps in further where poverty or separation leaves members unable to cope.
concepts.formula: need chain -- family plus community structures plus state institutions cover member needs
concepts.key_idea: With about a third of the world's poor living in India, state programmes and NGO effort must backstop struggling families.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe107.txt, Significance section and poverty box (approx lines 21-101)
question_patterns: why are services, institutions and programmes needed for children, youth and the elderly
why cannot the family alone meet all needs of its members
when does the state step in on behalf of family members
name the community structures that deliver specialised services
what distinguishes a holistic programme from a single need programme

solution_steps.explain: family first, community structures next, government and society as the final guarantor of a decent life

solution_steps.action: note the trigger for state action
solution_steps.explain: resource poor families and members cut off from family support

worked_examples.q: Which unit of society cannot deliver every specialised need alone: the family or the factory?

concepts.title: Vulnerability of Children, Youth and Elderly
concepts.definition: A person or group is vulnerable when adverse circumstances strike harder and more often; children qualify because rapid, interconnected development stalls when food, health, love and stimulation are missing, and youth and the elderly qualify through the special pressures and losses of their stages.
concepts.formula: vulnerability = unmet needs multiplied by stage specific exposure
concepts.key_idea: Two thirds of under fives face moderate or severe malnutrition, three million children live on the streets, and 17 million children work by official count.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe107.txt, vulnerability concept and children statistics (approx lines 103-161)
question_patterns: what does the term vulnerable mean
why are children, youth and the elderly called vulnerable groups
why does unmet need make a person vulnerable
state the statistics that show the needs of Indian children are unmet
why do adverse experiences leave a lasting mark on a young child

solution_steps.explain: greater likelihood and greater harm from adverse circumstances
children: fast linked development; youth: adult role pressures; elderly: health and support losses

worked_examples.q: A person or group struck harder by adverse circumstances is called what: vulnerable or volatile?

concepts.title: Juvenile Justice Act and Children in Need
concepts.section: Institutions, Programmes and Initiatives for Children
concepts.definition: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act of 2000, India's first juvenile justice framework, separates children who clash with the law from those needing care and protection -- the abandoned, the abused, the trafficked, disaster victims and others -- and demands a child friendly approach for their rehabilitation.
concepts.formula: two categories -- in conflict with law plus in need of care and protection
concepts.key_idea: The Act aligns with the Child Rights Convention and lists exactly which children count as needing care and protection.
question_patterns: which two categories of children does the Juvenile Justice Act 2000 cover
who is a juvenile in conflict with law
list the children considered in need of care and protection
what does the Juvenile Justice Act provide for rehabilitation
with which international convention is the Act compliant

solution_steps.explain: delinquency cases versus protection cases such as abandoned, abused or trafficked children
care, protection, treatment, development needs and child friendly adjudication

worked_examples.q: Which act of 2000 framed India's juvenile justice: the Juvenile Justice Act or the Consumer Act?

concepts.title: ICDS and the Anganwadi
concepts.section: Institutions, Programmes and Initiatives for Children
concepts.definition: The Integrated Child Development Services, the largest early childhood programme anywhere, bundles health, nutrition, stimulation and early learning for children under six with education for mothers, immunisation and growth monitoring, all delivered through the neighbourhood anganwadi centre.
concepts.formula: integrated bundle -- health plus nutrition plus preschool plus immunisation through one centre
concepts.key_idea: Over 41 million children are covered; non formal preschool runs for the three to six band and supplementary feeding for all under six.
question_patterns: what services does the ICDS deliver through the anganwadi
why is ICDS called the world's largest early childhood programme
which age groups does ICDS serve and how
what health inputs accompany the anganwadi programme
how does ICDS support pregnant and nursing mothers

solution_steps.explain: supplementary feeding, immunisation, vitamin A, growth monitoring, non formal preschool, maternal education
the anganwadi childcare centre

worked_examples.q: Which is the largest early childhood programme anywhere: ICDS or NSS?

concepts.title: SOS Children's Villages and Children's Homes
concepts.section: Institutions, Programmes and Initiatives for Children
concepts.definition: SOS Children's Villages give orphaned and abandoned children a trained mother, ten to fifteen siblings and a family style home clustered into a village, while the state runs observation homes for investigation stays, special homes for juveniles found guilty and children's homes for those with no traceable family.
concepts.formula: care ladder -- SOS family home to observation home to special home to children's home
concepts.key_idea: The first Indian SOS village opened in 1964; today about 6000 children live across 40 villages, and emergency relief after disasters often becomes permanent village capacity.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe107.txt, SOS Villages and three kinds of homes (approx lines 243-287)
question_patterns: describe the family approach of SOS Children's Villages
differentiate between observation homes, special homes and juvenile homes
who is the mother in an SOS home and how many children does she care for
since when has SOS worked in India and how large is its network now
what does the government provide for children in children's homes

solution_steps.explain: a mother, a sibling group, a village of such families woven into the local community

solution_steps.action: sort the three state homes by purpose
solution_steps.explain: temporary investigation stay, custodial sentence stay, long term care when family is gone

worked_examples.q: In SOS Children's Villages, orphaned children get a trained what: mother or manager?

concepts.title: Adoption and CARA
concepts.section: Institutions, Programmes and Initiatives for Children
concepts.definition: Adoption in India moved from a family bound religious practice to an institutionalised legal route; the Central Adoption Resource Authority, created on the Supreme Court's advice, writes the guidelines that guard the welfare and rights of adopted children, with NGOs running the delivery systems.
concepts.formula: adoption route -- policy plus CARA guidelines plus NGO delivery
concepts.key_idea: CARA exists to strengthen adoption rules and protect the child's interests.
question_patterns: how has adoption practice changed in India over time
what is CARA and why was it constituted
which bodies handle policy and which handle delivery of adoption
what safeguards guide adoption in India today

solution_steps.explain: within family custom to beyond family legal institution
governments make policy, CARA sets guidelines, NGOs operate the process

worked_examples.q: Which authority writes India's adoption guidelines: CARA or NASA?

concepts.title: Youth Vulnerability and Needs
concepts.definition: The National Youth Policy of 2014 places youth in the fifteen to twenty nine band, with adolescents at thirteen to nineteen; the stage strains under body changes, livelihood and marriage preparation, competition and peer pressure, and can slide into substance abuse, with rural, tribal, out of school, female, disabled and trafficked youth most exposed.
concepts.formula: age bands -- adolescents 13 to 19, youth 15 to 29
concepts.key_idea: Youth need education, training, jobs, shelter, health services, protection from exploitation and a voice in decisions that concern them.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe107.txt, youth vulnerability and needs (approx lines 304-355)
question_patterns: how does the National Youth Policy 2014 define youth
which age band names adolescents
why is youth called a vulnerable period
which groups of youth face special vulnerability
list the requisites for youth to become socially useful and economically productive
how do peer pressure and competition affect adolescents

solution_steps.explain: youth 15 to 29, adolescents 13 to 19
body and identity changes, livelihood stress, substance abuse, reproductive health risks, with sub groups most exposed

worked_examples.q: The National Youth Policy 2014 places youth in the fifteen to what age band: twenty-nine or ninety?

concepts.title: Youth Programmes in India
concepts.definition: Government channels youth energy through the National Service Scheme for college volunteers, the National Service Volunteer Scheme with Nehru Yuva Kendras for rural non student youth, adventure promotion, Scouts and Guides, the Commonwealth Youth Programme with its Chandigarh centre, and integration visits between states.
concepts.formula: programme set -- NSS plus NSVS plus adventure plus scouts plus Commonwealth plus integration
concepts.key_idea: The National Youth Policy was adopted in 2003 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports; Kendra activities build literacy, self reliance and scientific temper among rural youth.
question_patterns: describe the work of the National Service Scheme
how does the National Service Volunteer Scheme differ from NSS

how does the government promote national integration among youth

solution_steps.action: pair each programme with its audience
solution_steps.explain: college students, degree holders serving one or two years, rural non student youth, school age boys and girls
character, service, self reliance and integration

worked_examples.q: Which scheme channels college volunteers: the National Service Scheme or a defence scheme?

concepts.title: Elderly Vulnerability in India
concepts.definition: India counts senior citizens from sixty years; falling physiological reserves bring illness and disabilities like cataract, deafness and arthritis, while children moving away, city fragmentation of families, financial dependence and rising living costs leave many elders lonely and unsupported.
concepts.formula: risk stack -- health decline plus isolation plus money dependence
concepts.key_idea: Eighty per cent of the elderly live in villages, thirty per cent are below the poverty line, and most sixty plus Indians still work; the National Policy for Older Persons arrived in 1999.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe107.txt, elderly vulnerability and features (approx lines 451-516)
question_patterns: from which age is a person a senior citizen in India
why are the elderly more vulnerable to disease
which disabilities commonly accompany ageing
how do city life features reduce family support for the aged
what is meant by feminisation of the elderly population
state the special features of India's elderly population
which national policy addresses older persons and from when

solution_steps.explain: low reserves, cataract, nerve deafness, arthritis, loss of self care
empty nest, nuclear families, space and money pressures, changing values
many elders live fruitfully and most remain economically active, so they are a human resource

worked_examples.q: India counts senior citizens from what age: sixty or sixteen?

concepts.title: Programmes for the Elderly
concepts.definition: Public and voluntary effort runs old age homes, respite and continuous care homes, multi service day centres, mobile medicare units for remote areas, dementia day care, help lines, mental health and physiotherapy services, caregiver training, awareness drives and the National Old Age Pension Scheme for destitute persons above sixty five.
concepts.formula: programme set -- shelter plus health plus counselling plus pension plus awareness
concepts.key_idea: NOAPS pension reaches destitute seniors over sixty five who must prove age and destitution, and states may top up the amount.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe107.txt, programmes for the elderly list (approx lines 528-619)
question_patterns: name four programmes run for the elderly in India

solution_steps.explain: basic needs, institutional and non institutional care, health services, awareness and training, pension
destitute status, age above sixty five, proof documents, optional state top up

worked_examples.q: Which scheme pensions destitute seniors above sixty-five: NOAPS or NREGA?

concepts.title: Managing Institutions and Programmes
concepts.definition: Running a service organisation calls for people skills -- community ownership through participatory planning, private sector partnership, government liaison and harmonious internal relations -- plus administrative grip on finance, recruitment, records and equipment, all steered by a personal vision for the target group.
concepts.formula: manager profile -- people skills plus administrative skills plus vision
concepts.key_idea: Programmes planned with the community from the start earn the ownership that keeps them alive.
question_patterns: which four sets of people must a programme manager interact with
why is participatory planning called the pillar of effective programmes
how can the private sector support social programmes
list the administrative tasks involved in running an institution
what aspects must an entrepreneur weigh before starting a new organisation
why does a manager need vision

solution_steps.explain: community, private sector, government officials, colleagues and beneficiaries
finances, staff, space, records, registration, evaluation, all under a committed long term aim

worked_examples.q: Programmes planned with the community earn what: ownership or boredom?

concepts.title: Career Routes in Support Services
concepts.section: Preparing for a Career and Scope
concepts.definition: Entry runs through an undergraduate degree in Home Science, Social Work or allied social sciences, with IGNOU and state open universities adding a certificate in NGO management or a diploma in youth development work; careers open as founder of one's own institution, manager of an established one, functionary at any cadre, or researcher evaluating programmes.
concepts.formula: route -- degree plus open university courses to founder or manager or functionary or researcher
concepts.key_idea: Distance learning can run alongside a regular degree to build the specialised knowledge base.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe107.txt, knowledge base, courses and career avenues (approx lines 697-743)
question_patterns: which degrees prepare one for managing programmes for vulnerable groups
name the IGNOU courses useful for this career
what career avenues exist in the field of support services

solution_steps.explain: undergraduate degree plus optional certificate or diploma through open universities
set up, manage, serve, or research and evaluate

worked_examples.q: Entry runs through a degree in Home Science, Social Work or allied what: social sciences or sports?

concepts.title: SOS Village Capacity Arithmetic
concepts.definition: When a network states its total child count and its number of villages, the average load per village is the total divided by the count of villages.
concepts.key_idea: About 6000 children across 40 villages puts roughly 150 children in each village, housed in family homes of ten to fifteen.
question_patterns: an SOS network cares for 6000 children in 40 villages; find the average number of children per village
compute the average village load when the total children and the number of villages are stated
if an organisation houses T children across V villages, how many children does each village hold on average
find the mean number of children per village from the network's totals
a care network reports its strength and its village count; work out children per village

solution_steps.action: divide the children by the villages
solution_steps.explain: the quotient is the average village strength

worked_examples.q: 6000 children across 40 villages puts how many children per village on average: 150 or 1500?

concepts.title: Life Expectancy Gain
concepts.section: Why are the Elderly Vulnerable: life expectancy
concepts.definition: The rise in how long people live is the difference between the current expectancy figure and the historical one, and that gain is what swells the elderly population the chapter describes.
concepts.key_idea: Expectancy climbed from about 29 years in 1947 to 69.3 years for females and 65.8 for males in 2009-13.
question_patterns: female life expectancy rose from 29 years in 1947 to 69.3 years; how many years were gained
compute the gain in life expectancy when the historical and current figures are given
male expectancy stands at 65.8 years against about 29 in 1947; find the increase
by how many years did expectancy rise between the two quoted years
work out the improvement in years of life from the two expectancy values

solution_steps.action: subtract the old figure from the new one
solution_steps.explain: the difference is the gain in years of life

worked_examples.q: Life expectancy climbed from about 29 years in 1947 to what female figure by 2013: 69.3 or 29.3?

concepts.title: Elderly Population Shares
concepts.section: Why are the Elderly Vulnerable: population features
concepts.definition: Applying a stated percentage to the total elderly count prices each feature of the group: the village dwelling share, the poverty line share or any other quoted fraction becomes an absolute number of persons.
concepts.key_idea: Eighty per cent rural and thirty per cent poor are the two big shares to convert into head counts.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe107.txt, special features of the elderly (approx lines 461-475)
question_patterns: a district has 200000 elderly residents and 80 percent live in villages; compute the rural elderly count
if 30 percent of E million senior citizens are below the poverty line, calculate their number
convert a stated share of the elderly population into an absolute head count
a state has 500000 older persons; how many of them live below the poverty line at a 30 percent rate
find the number of village dwelling elders when the total and the rural percentage are given

solution_steps.action: apply the share to the total
solution_steps.explain: multiply the total by the percentage and divide by one hundred

worked_examples.q: Thirty percent of India's elderly are below the what line: poverty or finish?

concepts.title: School Retention Rate
concepts.definition: The share of enrolled children who stay the course to a later standard is the still enrolled count expressed as a percentage of the intake -- the survival measure behind the finding that only about a third of Standard I entrants reach Standard VIII.
concepts.key_idea: A little over one in three entrants survives to Standard VIII, so the rest drop out along the way.
question_patterns: of 120 children enrolled in Standard I only 40 reach Standard VIII; find the retention percentage
calculate the percentage of entrants who persist when the intake and the survivors are stated
a cohort of 300 shrinks to 90 by Standard VIII; what per cent stayed in school
compute the survival rate of an enrolled batch from the two counts
express the reaching count as a percentage of the enrolled count for a school cohort

solution_steps.explain: the ratio compares the persisting few with the starting batch
multiply by one hundred to state the retention rate

worked_examples.q: Only about a third of Standard I entrants reach which standard: VIII or XVIII?

worked_examples.question_pattern: A sixteen year old is caught for theft and a nine year old is found abandoned at a railway platform. Under which categories of the Juvenile Justice Act 2000 does each child fall and what happens next?

solution_template.explain: the sixteen year old is a juvenile in conflict with law; the abandoned nine year old is in need of care and protection
